acceptance_criteria: `Kernel::loft(&self, sections: &[Self::Shape], ruled: bool) -> Result<Self::Shape, KernelError>`, documented: the result is a closed solid through the sections' outer loops in the order given. `ruled` joins neighboring sections with straight-line (ruled) surfaces; otherwise one smooth surface passes through all sections. The doc comment cites OCCT's reference documentation for `BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections`. Implemented for `OcctKernel`. New shim code is `noexcept`, catches C++ exceptions, and rejects a result `BRepCheck_Analyzer` finds invalid. Every new `unsafe` call is in `ffi` with a SAFETY comment.

Tests (behind `occt`), volumes within 1e-6 relative, points within 1e-6: ruled square 20x20 z=0 to square 10x10 z=30: volume 7000; 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices; bbox (-10,-10,0)-(10,10,30). Ruled circle r10 z=0 to r5 z=20: volume 3500π/3; 3 faces; bbox (-10,-10,0)-(10,10,20). Three circles r10/r5/r10 at z=0/10/20: ruled volume 2·(π·10/3·175); smooth has same bbox and volume strictly between 500π and the ruled volume. Section faces unchanged afterwards.

Errors, each with a test and never a panic, all `InvalidInput` and checked before the backend: fewer than 2 sections; a section that is not a single planar face (e.g. a box solid); a section face with a hole (holes are out of scope).
Sections the backend can't loft (two equal squares at the same z) return an `Err`, not `Ok` or a panic, and the input faces are still usable afterwards.
No new dependencies. `swx-kernel` still has no workspace dependencies.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and so do the CI `swx-kernel (occt)` job commands.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
objective.description: M3-11a: Kernel loft through planar sections (ruled or smooth)
